originality.rationale: The 2018 independent-domination-polynomial source computes graph products and paths; the 2021 subdivision paper optimizes the number of subdivided edges, not maximal independent sets after full subdivision. The 2017 incidence-graph article establishes homotopy equivalence, which does not determine facet counts. The 2016 universal polynomial identities are not the stated forced-vertex bijection, forest recursion or induced-matching extremal equality. The 2019 family-specific scalar paper overlaps the operation but not the complete enumeration or general matching identity: its ladder formula disagrees with a direct four-vertex certificate on the three-rung ladder. Relevant published-record semantic searches found no equal or dominating statement. Unknown implicit equivalence remains possible.

value.rationale: The result enumerates every maximal independent set, not merely a minimum parameter, for full edge subdivisions of all finite simple graphs. It identifies an induced matching invariant controlling the minimum, characterizes all minimum sets by induced nontrivial tree components, and gives a finite-state polynomial-time enumerator for the full forest class. This is motivated by prior independent-domination subdivision work and has structural use beyond routine family substitution.
